# Installation

Install from the Bioconductor release compatible with your R installation.
Consult the [package page](https://bioconductor.org/packages/BreastSubtypeR/)
for the requirements of your selected channel:

```{r installation, eval = FALSE}
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("BreastSubtypeR")
```

Bioconductor release, Bioconductor devel, and GitHub are separate distribution
channels. GitHub may contain newer development changes that are not yet
available through Bioconductor. Consult the official
[release package page](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/BreastSubtypeR.html)
and [devel package page](https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/html/BreastSubtypeR.html)
for available versions and their R requirements. Use the R version compatible
with your selected Bioconductor release or devel environment; the package's
minimum R requirement does not replace that channel's requirements.
Matching version numbers do not guarantee matching source. After installing,
record `packageVersion("BreastSubtypeR")`, the installation channel and source
revision, and retain `sessionInfo()`.
This vignette describes its own built package; use `browseVignettes()` for
documentation matching an installed channel.

Use a separate R library and the R version required by
[Bioconductor devel](https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/html/BreastSubtypeR.html)
when choosing the development channel:

```{r installation-devel, eval = FALSE}
BiocManager::install(version = "devel")
BiocManager::install("BreastSubtypeR")
```

Alternatively, use a separate library configured for the GitHub source's
Bioconductor dependencies, install the development source, and inspect the
installed package version:

```{r installation-github, eval = FALSE}
if (!require("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("JohanHartmanGroupBioteam/BreastSubtypeR")
packageVersion("BreastSubtypeR")
```


# Citing BreastSubtypeR

If you use **BreastSubtypeR**, please cite:

- Yang Q., Hartman J., Sifakis E.G. (2025). *BreastSubtypeR: a unified R/Bioconductor package for intrinsic molecular subtyping in breast cancer research*. **NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics**, 7(4):lqaf131. <https://doi.org/10.1093/nargab/lqaf131>

For BibTeX/LaTeX, run in R:

```{r citation, eval = FALSE}
citation("BreastSubtypeR")
```


# Brief description

Breast cancer (BC) is a biologically heterogeneous disease with intrinsic molecular subtypes (e.g., Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-enriched, Basal-like, Normal-like) that inform biological interpretation and clinical decision-making. While clinical assays such as **Prosigna** provide standardized subtyping in the clinic, research implementations have proliferated and diverge in pre-processing, gene mapping, and algorithmic assumptions—reducing reproducibility and complicating cross-cohort analyses.

**BreastSubtypeR** consolidates multiple published gene-expression signature classifiers into a unified, assumption-aware Bioconductor package with: - a unified multi-method API (run many classifiers in one call), - **AUTO** mode for cohort-aware method selection, - standardized, method-specific pre-processing for multiple input types (raw counts, log2-normalized RNA-seq expression, log2-processed arrays), - Entrez ID–based probe/gene mapping, - and a local Shiny app (`iBreastSubtypeR`) for non-programmers.


## Features

-   **Unified interface for published methods:** consolidates PAM50 variants, AIMS, ssBC/sspbc, and others under one consistent API.
-   **Run multiple methods at once (`BS_Multi`):** execute several classifiers in a single call and compare results side by side.
-   **AUTO (cohort-aware selection):** selects methods using implemented receptor-annotation and subgroup-size rules; returns per-method calls.
-   **Method-specific pre-processing:** routes raw RNA-seq counts, or log2-normalized RNA-seq/microarray/nCounter expression with `RawCounts = FALSE`.
-   **Robust mapping:** Entrez ID–based gene mapping with conflict resolution.
-   **Local Shiny app (`iBreastSubtypeR`):** point-and-click analysis in your local R session.
-   **Reproducibility:** Bioconductor distribution, unit tests, vignettes, and `SummarizedExperiment` compatibility.

## Implemented approaches

The package includes implementations of commonly used subtyping methods (NC-based and SSP-based):

| **Method id** | **Short description** | **Group** | **Reference** |
|------------------|-------------------|------------------|------------------|
| `parker.original` | Original PAM50 by Parker et al., 2009 | NC-based | [Parker et al., 2009](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2008.18.1370) |
| `genefu.scale` | PAM50 implementation as in the genefu R package (scaled version) | NC-based | [Gendoo et al., 2016](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btv693) |
| `genefu.robust` | PAM50 implementation as in the genefu R package (robust version) | NC-based | [Gendoo et al., 2016](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btv693) |
| `cIHC` | Conventional ER-balancing using immunohistochemistry (IHC) | NC-based | [Ciriello et al., 2015](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2015.09.033) |
| `cIHC.itr` | Iterative version of cIHC | NC-based | [Curtis et al., 2012](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature10983) |
| `PCAPAM50` | Selects IHC-defined ER subsets, then uses Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to create ESR1 expression-based ER-balancing | NC-based | [Raj-Kumar et al., 2019](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-44339-4) |
| `ssBC` | Subgroup-specific gene-centering PAM50 | NC-based | [Zhao et al., 2015](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13058-015-0520-4) |
| `ssBC.v2` | Updated subgroup-specific gene-centering PAM50 | NC-based | [Fernandez-Martinez et al., 2020](https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.20.01276), [2024](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaoncol.2023.7304) |
| `AIMS` | Absolute Intrinsic Molecular Subtyping (AIMS) method | SSP-based | [Paquet & Hallett, 2015](https://doi.org/10.1093/jnci/dju357) |
| `sspbc` | Single-Sample Predictors for Breast Cancer (AIMS adaptation) | SSP-based | [Staaf et al., 2022](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41523-022-00465-3) |

Zhao et al. (2015) introduced subgroup-specific gene centering.
Fernandez-Martinez et al. (2020) described its HER2/ER-specific application.
The packaged `ssBC.v2` quantiles match the public `SIGMA.txt` reference in the
[Perou Lab normalization repository](https://github.com/perou-lab/PAM50_ER_HER2_normalization),
associated with Fernandez-Martinez et al. (2024). Across the 50 PAM50 genes,
`ER.v2` uses `ERneg_HER2neg`, `ERpos_HER2neg`, `HER2pos_ERneg` and
`HER2pos_ERpos`; `TN.v2` uses `TNBC`. The original `ER` and `TN` quantiles
remain separate. See `?BreastSubtypeRobj` for the pinned numerical reference.


**For research use.** Package outputs are not clinical assay results and do
not replace validated clinical diagnostics.

# Quick start

The examples below use small example datasets shipped with the package. For your own data, provide a `SummarizedExperiment` **with clinical metadata in `colData`** (e.g., `PatientID`, ER/HER2; for ROR: `TSIZE`, `NODE`).

`OSLO2EMIT0obj$se_obj` contains expression values for 356 gene features from
102 OSLO2-EMIT0 samples, calculated as `log2(FPKM + 1)` from
library-protocol-adjusted FPKM. Clinical metadata are stored in `colData`,
and feature annotations in `rowData`. The source is
`OSLO2EMIT0.103.genematrix_noNeg.Rdata` in Mendeley Data, version 3
([Vallon-Christersson, 2023](https://doi.org/10.17632/yzxtxn4nmd.3)).
See `?OSLO2EMIT0obj` for the packaged example's source and structure.

```{r pkgs-and-data, message=FALSE}
library(BreastSubtypeR)

# Example data
data("BreastSubtypeRobj")
data("OSLO2EMIT0obj")
```

**1) Map & prepare (method-specific pre-processing + mapping)**

```{r map and prepare, eval=TRUE}
# Pre-processing: automatically apply tailored normalization, map probes/IDs to Entrez,
# and (optionally) impute missing values
data_input <- Mapping(
    OSLO2EMIT0obj$se_obj,
    method = "max", # mapping strategy (example)
    RawCounts = FALSE,
    impute = TRUE,
    verbose = FALSE
)
```

***Notes***

-   `Mapping()` prepares expression inputs for downstream subtyping functions by:
    -   automatically applying tailored normalization workflows depending on input type
        -   **Raw RNA-seq counts (+ gene lengths):** converted to log2-CPM (upper-quartile normalized) for NC-based methods; converted to linear FPKM for SSP-based methods.\
        -   **Precomputed RNA-seq FPKM (log₂-transformed):** used directly for NC-based methods; back-transformed to linear scale (`2^x`) for SSP-based methods.\
        -   **Microarray/nCounter (log₂-processed):** used directly for NC-based methods; back-transformed to linear scale (`2^x`) for SSP-based methods.\
    -   resolving probe/ID → Entrez mappings,\
    -   selecting or collapsing multiple probes per gene (`method` argument),\
    -   optionally imputing missing marker values,\
    -   and returning a packaged object ready for `BS_Multi` or single-method callers.
-   See `?Mapping` for the full parameter list (e.g., `RawCounts`, `method`, `impute`, `verbose`) and [Methods (Sections 2.3–2.4) in the paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/nargab/lqaf131) for a complete description of the input/normalization pipeline.

## Descriptive input coverage

`InputCoverage()` reports the current processed inputs independently of which
methods are selected or run. It uses the same calculation as the current
GitHub Shiny coverage table. Current GitHub source contains `InputCoverage()`;
older Bioconductor builds may not. Consult your selected channel's
[package page](https://bioconductor.org/packages/BreastSubtypeR/) before running
this additional example.

```{r input-coverage, eval=TRUE}
coverage <- InputCoverage(data_input)
coverage
```

The four rows are **NC-based (PAM50)**, **AIMS**, **SSPBC (ssp.subtype)** and
**SSPBC (ssp.pam50)**. Denominators are derived from the bundled references
and fitted models: respectively 50, 151, 153 and 216 unique genes; rule
counts are not applicable, 100, 84 and 120. All three NC rule columns are `NA`.

Represented genes have matching identifiers even when their expression is
zero or missing. An evaluable rule is a native gene-pair comparison with a
nonmissing TRUE or FALSE result; a false rule is still evaluable. Missing
genes and NA/NaN comparisons can make rules unavailable. Native zero, tie,
infinity and duplicate-handling behavior is preserved. The minimum and
maximum evaluable counts form a range across samples when they differ.

These are **processed-input** diagnostics. `Mapping(impute = TRUE)` may have
already imputed values, and coverage cannot reconstruct which measurements
were originally observed. Coverage is not prediction reliability, does not
impose thresholds or exclude methods, and does not assess calibration
feasibility. NC coverage concerns the shared PAM50 subtype reference, not
every gene or component used in ROR calculations. See `?InputCoverage`.

The bundled AIMS setting `k = 20` identifies its fitted-model setting and
output column. Its complete `all.pairs` vector and fitted naive Bayes tables
contain 100 rule predictors involving 151 unique genes. Thus `k` is not the
total rule denominator. SSPBC uses `k = 21` for its 84-rule four-class model
and `k = 24` for its 120-rule five-class model. No model is altered by reporting.

**2) Multi-method run (user-defined)**

```{r multi-method run, eval=TRUE}
methods <- c("parker.original", "PCAPAM50", "sspbc")

res <- BS_Multi(
    data_input = data_input,
    methods = methods,
    Subtype = FALSE,
    hasClinical = FALSE
)

# Per-sample calls (rows = samples; columns = methods and entropy)
head(res$res_subtypes, 5)
```

**3) AUTO mode (cohort-aware selection) + visualize**

AUTO selects a set of methods using implemented receptor-annotation and
subgroup-size rules. It returns per-method calls, not a consensus prediction.
Selection does not establish complete input adequacy or clinical validity.

```{r auto mode and visualization, eval=TRUE}
res_auto <- BS_Multi(
    data_input = data_input,
    methods = "AUTO",
    Subtype = FALSE,
    hasClinical = FALSE
)

# visualize multi-method output and concordance
Vis_Multi(res_auto$res_subtypes)
```

***AUTO logic (clarifications)***

-   **TNBC cohorts** take precedence when all evaluable TN annotations indicate TN. At least 18 TN samples enable **ssBC and ssBC.v2**, plus SSP-based methods (AIMS, sspbc); smaller TN cohorts run SSP only.
-   **HER2+ cohort detection**: a cohort is treated as HER2+ when it has at least one evaluable HER2 value and **every** evaluable HER2 value is HER2+. The test reads the HER2 column alone, so one HER2- sample ends the HER2+ classification whether or not its ER value is known, and a sample whose HER2 value is missing or equivocal ("2+") neither creates nor removes a HER2+ cohort. AUTO reports how many samples had no evaluable HER2 value and therefore took no part in the decision.  
-   In this **HER2+ cohort** route, AUTO enables **ssBC.v2** plus SSP when there are at least 8 ER+/HER2+ samples or 9 ER-/HER2+ samples; otherwise it runs SSP only. This route does not additionally require the total-ER minima of 15 and 18.
-   **Cohorts without any evaluable HER2 value** are not treated as HER2+; they follow the ER-based rules (ssBC.v2 then returns NA for every sample).  
-   For remaining cohorts, both ER totals below their minima run SSP only. When only one ER group reaches its minimum, its HER2 subgroups determine whether **ssBC and/or ssBC.v2** run alongside SSP: both HER2 subgroups reaching their minima enable both methods, while just one enables ssBC.v2.
-   **Mixed cohorts** with at least 15 ER+ and 18 ER- samples run ten methods when `0.39 < n_ERpos / (n_ERpos + n_ERneg) < 0.69`. These are strict inequalities: at or outside either boundary, eight methods run, excluding `parker.original` and `genefu.scale`. Both branches include `cIHC.itr`.
-   **Minimum sample group sizes (defaults used by AUTO)**:
    -   ER+ total: `n_ERpos_threshold = 15`
    -   ER− total: `n_ERneg_threshold = 18`
    -   TNBC total: `n_TN_threshold = 18` (currently aligned with ER−)
    -   ER+ subgroups (HER2+ or HER2−): `n_ERposHER2pos_threshold = n_ERposHER2neg_threshold = round(n_ERpos_threshold / 2)`
    -   ER− subgroups (HER2+ or HER2−): `n_ERnegHER2pos_threshold = n_ERnegHER2neg_threshold = round(n_ERneg_threshold / 2)`

**Notes.** Thresholds are *selection gates* for method eligibility; they do not force a consensus call.

**Provenance & future updates.** The ER+ (15) and ER- (18) cohort minimums are simulation-based defaults. ER/HER2 subgroup thresholds (approx. half of each ER total) are heuristic and may be updated as additional simulation studies are completed. For TNBC, we currently use the ER- minimum (18) as the cohort cutoff; TN-specific thresholds may likewise be refined in future releases.

**4) Single-method run**

PAM50 (NC-based)

```{r pam50 subtyping, eval=TRUE}
res_pam <- BS_parker(
    se_obj = data_input$se_NC, # object prepared for NC-based methods
    calibration = "Internal",
    internal = "medianCtr",
    Subtype = FALSE,
    hasClinical = FALSE
)
```

AIMS (SSP-based)

```{r aims subtyping, eval=TRUE}
res_aims <- BS_AIMS(data_input$se_SSP)
```

AIMS also accepts one sample. Map that sample and retain its identifiers:

```{r aims-single-sample, eval=TRUE}
one_sample <- Mapping(OSLO2EMIT0obj$se_obj[, 1], RawCounts = FALSE)
aims_one <- BS_AIMS(one_sample$se_SSP)
aims_one$cl
stopifnot(
    identical(dim(aims_one$cl), c(1L, 1L)),
    identical(rownames(aims_one$cl), colnames(one_sample$se_SSP)),
    identical(dim(aims_one$prob), c(1L, 1L)),
    identical(dim(aims_one$all.probs[["20"]]), c(1L, 5L))
)
```

The `cl` component contains subtype calls and `prob` contains the probabilities
of those assigned calls. Both are sample-by-one matrices with sample IDs as
row names; `all.probs[["20"]]` has one row per sample and five subtype columns.
These dimensions are preserved for one or many samples.

## Iterative cIHC and ER balancing

`BS_cIHC.itr()` defaults to 100 iterations and `er_subsample = "target"`.
Its `ratio = 54 / 64` is the target number of ER-positive samples per
ER-negative sample, not the ER-positive fraction used by AUTO. The ratio must
be one finite, strictly positive number. Values above 1 are allowed in target
mode. Write `54 / 64`, not the R sequence `54:64`.

Each iteration subsamples the group over-represented relative to the target,
without replacement, to `ceiling(ratio * n_ERneg)` ER+ samples or
`ceiling(n_ERpos / ratio)` ER- samples, retaining the other group. A cohort
already at the target within this rounding is used in full. For example, the
default target gives 34 ER+ : 40 ER- from 100 ER+ : 40 ER-, and 40 ER+ : 48 ER-
from 40 ER+ : 100 ER-.

```{r cihc-iteration-settings, eval=TRUE}
# Ten iterations keep this example quick; the function default is 100.
res_itr <- BS_cIHC.itr(
    se_obj = data_input$se_NC,
    iteration = 10,
    ratio = 54 / 64,
    er_subsample = "target",
    Subtype = FALSE,
    hasClinical = FALSE
)
head(res_itr$BS.all)
```

For reproduction of BreastSubtypeR 1.5.5 and earlier,
`er_subsample = "larger"` subsamples the numerically larger ER group to
`ceiling(ratio * n_smaller)`, retaining the smaller group. In that legacy mode,
the ratio cannot exceed `n_larger / n_smaller`. With the default ratio and
otherwise identical inputs, seed and settings, target and legacy modes agree
when ER+ samples are at least as numerous as ER- samples. This equivalence is
not guaranteed for other ratios. `BS_Multi(er_subsample = "larger")` passes
the legacy choice to cIHC.itr only; AUTO selection is unchanged.

## Four- versus five-class results and ROR

NC methods retain their five-class calls and add a four-class call when
`Subtype = TRUE`. `BS_Multi()` likewise always returns the five-class table
`res_subtypes`; `Subtype = TRUE` adds `res_subtypes.Subtype`. Both tables have
sample IDs as row names, one column per method and an entropy column. AIMS is
a five-class predictor with no four-class model: its Normal calls are set to
`NA` only in the four-class multi-method summary. The original AIMS calls are
retained in the five-class summary and per-method results. SSPBC uses its
four-class `ssp.subtype` model for the four-class summary.

NC methods return ROR-S and ROR-P scores and risk groups in `score.ROR` without
requiring clinical covariates. Setting `hasClinical = TRUE` requires `TSIZE`
and `NODE` columns in `colData` and adds clinical ROR outputs. `TSIZE` is binary
(0 for at most 2 cm, 1 for more than 2 cm); it enters ROR-C and both ROR-PC
scores. No numerical ROR score uses `NODE`.

For `NODE`, supply the actual nonnegative integer number of positive lymph
nodes as numeric values when available. Only the additional risk group
`ROR-PC Group (Subtype + Clinic + Prolif.Subtype)` distinguishes 0, 1--3 and
4 or more positive nodes. With nonmissing `TSIZE`, 4 or more nodes receive high
risk; 0 and 1--3 use different score cutoffs. Binary 0/1 coding is accepted,
but cannot distinguish 1--3 from 4 or more positive nodes. The current R API
checks numeric type without enforcing nonnegative integer counts.

In the R API, `NA` in `NODE` makes only this additional risk group missing.
`NA` in `TSIZE` makes all clinical ROR scores and groups missing, while ROR-S
and ROR-P remain available. These are missing values within required columns;
the columns themselves must still be supplied. The additional subtype-specific
ROR-PC group now uses inclusive upper boundaries: for NODE = 0, scores <= 40
are low, > 40 through 60 are intermediate, and > 60 are high; for 1--3 nodes,
the corresponding boundaries are 15 and 40. Raw scores are not rounded before
grouping. This resolves [issue #154](https://github.com/JohanHartmanGroupBioteam/BreastSubtypeR/issues/154)
and leaves the original Parker risk groups unchanged.
Method-specific return components are documented in their
help pages. These are research-use outputs, not a clinical assay result.

# Guidance & best practices

## Input types

- Provide **one** of the following as input:
    - raw counts **plus** gene lengths (for internal calculation of CPM/FPKM),
    - log2-normalized RNA-seq expression (for example, log2(FPKM+1)),
    - log2-processed microarray/nCounter matrices (e.g., RMA).
- Set `RawCounts = TRUE` for raw RNA-seq counts with gene lengths in the
  `Length` annotation column. With `RawCounts = FALSE`, supply log2-normalized
  expression: it is used directly for NC methods and back-transformed with
  `2^x` for SSP methods. This setting does not detect or log-transform a
  supplied linear FPKM/TPM matrix.
- Include `probe` and `ENTREZID` in `rowData`, and sample identifiers in
  `colData$PatientID` matching the assay columns. Receptor fields are required
  by AUTO and methods that use them; see `?Mapping` for their accepted coding.
- `BreastSubtypeR` routes the supplied input to the appropriate, **method-specific** pre-processing pipeline — see `?Mapping`, `?BS_Multi` and [Methods (Section 2.3) in the paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/nargab/lqaf131) for details.

## When to use `AUTO`

- Use `methods = "AUTO"` (i.e. `BS_Multi(methods = "AUTO", ...)`) for exploratory datasets or cohorts of unknown / skewed composition.
- AUTO applies its documented cohort-selection rules; it does not validate
  model-wide gene/rule adequacy or clinical applicability.
- To study a published method, run the corresponding single-method
  implementation directly (for example, `BS_parker()`). Clinical validation
  requires paired clinical-assay data; calling a function alone is insufficient.

## Interpretation

These outputs answer different questions:

| Output | Meaning in this implementation | Limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input coverage | Identifier representation and native rule evaluability in processed matrices | Does not establish reliability, calibration feasibility or measured-versus-imputed provenance |
| Entropy | Raw Shannon entropy in bits, `-sum(p * log2(p))`, over available per-method calls | Measures disagreement, not predictive confidence or accuracy |
| Parker `Confidence` | `round(1 - p, 2)`, where `p` is the Spearman correlation-test p-value between the processed sample and its assigned centroid over matched, complete gene pairs | A correlation-test summary, not a calibrated subtype probability |
| SSP model probabilities | Fitted naive Bayes `predict(..., type = "raw")` values; `prob` is the assigned class probability and `all.probs` retains class probabilities | Conditional on the fitted model and native handling of available rule inputs; not clinical reliability |

Missing calls are excluded from entropy. Zero means agreement among the
contributing calls, including a single available call; `NA` means no calls
contributed. Low entropy from a small contributing set is weak evidence of
agreement across methods. Five- and four-class summaries use their own calls.

Parker `Confidence` is missing when a valid test cannot be computed (for
example, insufficient or constant matched values). It differs from centroid
correlation itself and from AIMS/SSPBC posterior probabilities. None of these
quantities substitutes for external predictive or clinical validation.
AUTO continues to return separate method calls without consensus voting.

# Shiny app

For users new to R, we offer an intuitive Shiny app for interactive molecular subtyping.

## Launch the local Shiny app

```{r launch shiny, eval = FALSE}
BreastSubtypeR::iBreastSubtypeR() # interactive GUI (local)
```

If needed, install UI dependencies and re-run:

```{r installui dependencies, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib"))
```

The launcher runs the Shiny application locally in your R session. Uploaded
inputs are processed by that local application; remotely hosting Shiny is a
separate deployment with different data-handling responsibilities.

**What you can do**:\
- Upload expression, clinical, and feature-annotation tables (clinical lives in `colData`).\
- Run single methods, or run multiple classifiers at once with `BS_Multi` and `AUTO` enabled for cohort-aware selection.\
- Choose 5-class (incl. Normal-like) or 4-class (AIMS is 5-class only).\
- Inspect per-sample concordance (entropy), heatmap and pie summaries.\
- Export current Calls-only results, or Full metrics for supported single NC methods. AUTO, AIMS and sspbc provide Calls-only exports. NC Full metrics include ROR-S/ROR-P; enabling **Use clinical variables (ROR)** with valid numeric `TSIZE`/`NODE` adds clinical ROR-C/ROR-PC outputs. AUTO exports calls and entropy with clinical ROR disabled.

## Preprocessing, prediction and downloads

Upload all three tables: expression with feature IDs in the first column and
sample IDs as column names, clinical metadata with `PatientID`, and annotation
with `probe` and `ENTREZID`. The application aligns overlapping sample and
feature identifiers. Choose normalized **log2** expression or raw RNA-seq
counts; raw-count annotation must also contain gene lengths in `Length` (bp).
Alternatively, load the bundled example below. Click **Preprocess & map**,
select a method and its settings, then run subtyping. In current GitHub main,
the **Input coverage** table appears after successful mapping and describes
the current processed inputs, including possible imputation. It reports all
four input models independently of method selection. Replacing or invalidating
mapped inputs hides the table; a coverage-reporting error is informative and
does not change prediction state.

Replacing any expression, clinical or annotation file, reloading the example,
or changing the data type clears the mapped inputs, predictions, plots and
downloads. Preprocess and run again. Changes to relevant prediction settings clear old
predictions, plots and downloads but retain valid mapped inputs when no
remapping is needed. A failed prediction also clears previous results.

Before a current successful prediction exists, the app asks you to run
subtyping and offers no active download control. A successful run restores
its plots and supported export choices. Unsupported Full metrics exports are
identified explicitly. Server-side checks also reject direct requests to old
download URLs after invalidation; an intentional HTTP 500 rejection from such
a URL does not mean the Shiny session has disconnected.

For Shiny cIHC.itr, the ratio follows target-mode semantics above. Iterations
default to 100, with a minimum of 10 and a control step of 10. Any whole number
from 10 through 2147483647 is accepted, including 11; the step is not a
multiple-of-ten requirement. Missing, nonnumeric, nonfinite, fractional or
out-of-range iterations, and missing, nonnumeric, nonfinite or nonpositive
ratios, produce an actionable error without disconnecting the session.
Correct the setting and rerun without reloading the page or remapping valid
inputs. These Shiny input checks do not change the underlying R API or its
default settings.


## Example data (for Shiny & scripts)

The Shiny UI provides a **“Load example data…”** button that preloads a small
demo cohort (expression, clinical, annotation). After loading, click
**Preprocess & map** (Step 1), then proceed to analyses (Step 2).

The Shiny expression file contains the same 356 features and 102 samples as
`OSLO2EMIT0obj$se_obj`, with `log2(FPKM + 1)` expression agreeing at text
serialization precision. The expression values are not binary-identical.
The Shiny annotation table covers 19,675 genes, including all 356 packaged
features with matching annotations. Its clinical table has 12 fields rather
than the packaged object's six; sample identifiers align, but PR labels use
`Negative`/`Positive` instead of `PR-`/`PR+`. The full metadata tables therefore
differ. Numerical agreement does not establish the exact historical
generating or export script.

Programmatic access to the same Shiny files:

```{r load example data, eval = FALSE}
exdir <- system.file("RshinyTest", package = "BreastSubtypeR")
gex <- file.path(exdir, "OSLO2EMIT0_GEX_log2.FPKM.txt")
clin <- file.path(exdir, "OSLO2EMIT0_clinical.txt")
anno <- file.path(exdir, "OSLO2EMIT0_anno.txt")
file.exists(gex)
file.exists(clin)
file.exists(anno)
```

# Limitations

BreastSubtypeR harmonizes many published, signature-based classifiers but has known limitations:\

- It is not a clinical-grade replacement for assays like Prosigna; 
clinical validation requires paired clinical assay data.\

- AUTO selects methods using implemented cohort rules and returns per-method
  calls without a consensus prediction.
